---
title: "C. Build and inspect a Zarr cube"
---

This page turns the remapped interim NetCDF files into a compressed, chunked and sharded Zarr v3 store, then opens a small selection for inspection.

## 1. Check the interim files

The builder expects NetCDF files under data/interim/ and dimensions named time, lat and lon.

~~~bash
find data/interim -name '*_processed.nc' -type f
cdo -s sinfo data/interim/METREF/2020/06/example_processed.nc
~~~

Replace the example filename with one of your actual outputs. Confirm time and coordinate dimensions and inspect valid values before building the cube. If your files use x and y, update the dimension names and chunk configuration in code/build_zarr_cube.py.

## 2. Build the cube

From the repository root:

~~~bash
uv run python code/build_zarr_cube.py
~~~

The script uses xarray to open multiple files by coordinates and Dask for lazy/chunked processing. It writes to:

~~~text
data/zarr/example.zarr/
~~~

The current builder requires **Zarr 3**. Use a Python environment that resolves Zarr 3 as required by the script. The script removes an existing output store before rebuilding; copy or rename any output you need to keep first.

## 3. Understand chunks, shards and compression

The script currently starts with:

~~~python
INNER_CHUNKS = {"time": 1, "lat": 256, "lon": 256}
SHARD_CHUNKS = {"time": 10, "lat": 512, "lon": 512}
COMPRESSOR = BloscCodec(cname="zstd", clevel=5, shuffle="shuffle")
~~~

| Setting | Role | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| Inner chunks | Small independently readable blocks | Smaller blocks help selective reads but add metadata/overhead |
| Shards | Group storage for multiple inner chunks | Larger shards reduce object count but may make writes/updates coarser |
| Zstd compression | Reduces stored bytes | Higher compression can use more CPU |

These are initial values, not universal optima. Benchmark common access patterns: a map at one time, a point/area time series, and a small regional subset.

## 4. Open and inspect

~~~python
import xarray as xr

ds = xr.open_zarr("data/zarr/metref_sample_1month.zarr", consolidated=False)
print(ds)
print(list(ds.data_vars))
~~~

Select a time slice and a point time series:

~~~python
variable = next(iter(ds.data_vars))
map_at_time = ds[variable].isel(time=0)
point_series = ds[variable].isel(lat=100, lon=100)
~~~

These indices are examples only. Check the coordinates at the selected indices, dimension ordering, variable units, and timestamp before interpreting a plot. The project plotting utilities are in code/plot_utils/; see their README for import and usage examples.

## 5. Validation after writing

The builder reopens the output store and computes a small sample statistic. Also check:

- expected dimensions, coordinate ranges and time count;
- data-variable names and attributes/units;
- valid-value coverage in a few known maps and time slices;
- representative values against the interim NetCDF source;
- whether map/time-series reads perform acceptably for your use case.

A successful Zarr write checks storage/readability, not the scientific correctness of source values or remapping.

## 6. Scaling beyond the sample

For a priority subset, measure runtime, peak memory, interim and Zarr sizes, valid coverage and read speed. Expand to a larger region or a 2,000 km corridor by processing grid-aligned spatial tiles and time batches. Add a remapping margin at tile boundaries, then remove duplicate edge cells from the final grid.

Parallelize independent NetCDF files or tiles up to the measured CPU, memory, storage and network limits of the available workstation/VM. Use isolated temporary stores or non-overlapping Zarr regions; avoid concurrent writes to the same chunk/shard. Keep a manifest and rerun only failed batches. Re-benchmark chunks and shards on the larger workload.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Checks |
|---|---|
| No interim files | Check downloader output, input path and CDO log |
| Many NaNs after remapping | Compare raw AOI, crop bounds and target-grid bounds; inspect fill values and source QA |
| Zarr dimension error | Print ds.sizes; rename coordinates or change chunk dimensions |
| Zarr version error | Check uv run python -c "import zarr; print(zarr.__version__)"; script needs version 3 or newer |
| Slow writes or reads | Check RAM/disk I/O, chunk and shard sizes, and number of parallel tasks |
| Output already exists | Builder replaces its output; back up the store or change OUTPUT in the script |

## Next steps

After the pilot is validated, add quality-aware masks, explicit coverage thresholds, provenance metadata, reproducible configuration records, and automated tests for representative source files.
